summary:
Dancing with the SARs is an educational Earth-observation game inspired by the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission. It helps students learn about Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), radar observations, and environmental changes through an interactive game. Dancing_with_the_SARs_NISAR_SINGLE_PLAYER_FINAL.html
SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a remote-sensing technology that uses radar signals to observe the Earth's surface. Unlike ordinary optical cameras, SAR can collect information during both day and night and can work under many cloud conditions. It can be used to study floods, forests, weather conditions, and land changes. Dancing_with_the_SARs_NISAR_SINGLE_PLAYER_FINAL.html
NISAR stands for NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar. It is a joint Earth-observation mission by NASA and ISRO. Its radar instruments observe changes in land, ice, and ecosystems. Dancing_with_the_SARs_NISAR_SINGLE_PLAYER_FINAL.html
The game includes a Tamil Nadu SAR Map, where players can explore locations such as Chennai, Kanchipuram, Cuddalore, Cauvery Delta, Nilgiris, and the Gulf of Mannar. Dancing_with_the_SARs_NISAR_SINGLE_PLAYER_FINAL.html
Players complete 5 mission levels, answer science-based questions, earn points, and unlock a Bonus Mission after completing all five levels. Dancing_with_the_SARs_NISAR_SINGLE_PLAYER_FINAL.html
Overall, the project combines space science, and gaming to make learning about SAR and the NISAR mission simple and engaging. Dancing_with_the_SARs_NISAR_SINGLE_PLAYER_FINAL.html
details:
Our project, “Dancing with the SARs,” is an interactive single-player web game inspired by Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites. The game makes learning about SAR technology more engaging through a simple and fun gameplay experience.

The main goal of the project is to help users understand the importance of SAR satellites and how they can observe Earth in different conditions. The project combines education and entertainment, making a complex space-science topic easier and more interesting for students and the general public.

We developed the project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The game includes interactive elements, animations, game logic, and a user-friendly interface. We focused on creativity, simplicity, visual appeal, and ease of use while designing the game.

Our team considered factors such as educational value, user experience, accessibility, creativity, performance, and the ability to explain SAR concepts through gameplay. Overall, the project aims to turn learning about Earth observation and SAR technology into an enjoyable interactive experience.
